sanskrit: te vimānair mahātmāno jvalitair jvalanaprabhāḥ devasyānumate 'gacchan gaṅgādvāram iti śrutiḥ
english: Those great-souled ones, in blazing chariots that shone like fire, departed with the god's leave for the Gate of the Gaṅgā — so the tradition tells.

sanskrit: prasthitā devatā dṛṣṭvā śailarājasutā tadā uvāca vacanaṃ sādhvī devaṃ paśupatiṃ patim
english: Seeing the gods set forth, the daughter of the king of mountains, that virtuous lady, then spoke these words to her lord, the god Paśupati.

sanskrit: bhagavan kva nu yānty ete devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ brūhi tattvena tattvajña saṃśayo me mahān ayam
english: "Blessed lord, where do these gods go, with Śakra at their head? Tell me truly, O knower of truth, for great is this doubt of mine."

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca dakṣo nāma mahābhāge prajānāṃ patir uttamaḥ hayamedhena yajate tatra yānti divaukasaḥ
english: Maheśvara said: "O greatly blessed one, there is a foremost lord of creatures named Dakṣa; he is performing the horse-sacrifice, and it is there the dwellers in heaven are bound."

sanskrit: umā uvāca yajñam etaṃ mahābhāga kimarthaṃ nābhigacchasi kena vā pratiṣedhena gamanaṃ te na vidyate
english: Umā said: "O greatly blessed one, why do you not go to this sacrifice? By what prohibition is your going barred?"

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca surair eva mahābhāge sarvam etad anuṣṭhitam yajñeṣu sarveṣu mama na bhāga upakalpitaḥ
english: Maheśvara said: "O greatly blessed one, it is the gods themselves who have arranged all this: in none of the sacrifices has a share been appointed for me."

sanskrit: pūrvopāyopapannena mārgeṇa varavarṇini na me surāḥ prayacchanti bhāgaṃ yajñasya dharmataḥ
english: "By a course sanctioned by ancient usage, O fair-complexioned one, the gods do not, as dharma requires, render unto me a share of the sacrifice."

sanskrit: umā uvāca bhagavan sarvabhūteṣu prabhavābhyadhiko guṇaiḥ ajeyaś cāpradhṛṣyaś ca tejasā yaśasā śriyā
english: Umā said: "Blessed lord, among all beings you surpass them in power and in virtues; unconquerable and unassailable you are, in splendor, in fame, in majesty."

sanskrit: anena te mahābhāga pratiṣedhena bhāgataḥ atīva duḥkham utpannaṃ vepathuś ca mamānagha
english: "By this exclusion from your share, O greatly blessed and sinless one, an overwhelming grief has arisen in me, and a trembling besides."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktvā tu sā devī devaṃ paśupatiṃ patim tūṣṇīṃbhūtābhavad rājan dahyamānena cetasā
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus to her lord, the god Paśupati, that goddess fell silent, O king, with a heart consumed by grief.

sanskrit: atha devyā mataṃ jñātvā hṛdgataṃ yac cikīrṣitam sa samājñāpayām āsa tiṣṭha tvam iti nandinam
english: Then, perceiving the mind of the goddess and what purpose lay hidden in her heart, he gave his command to Nandin: "Stand ready!"

sanskrit: tato yogabalaṃ kṛtvā sarvayogeśvareśvaraḥ taṃ yajñaṃ sumahātejā bhīmair anucarais tadā sahasā ghātayām āsa devadevaḥ pinākadhṛk
english: Then, summoning the force of yoga, the lord of all lords of yoga, that god of gods of mighty splendor, the bearer of the Pināka, with his terrible attendants suddenly had that sacrifice struck down.

sanskrit: ke cin nādān amuñcanta ke cid dhāsāṃś ca cakrire rudhireṇāpare rājaṃs tatrāgniṃ samavākiran
english: Some let loose roars, some burst into laughter, and others, O king, drenched the sacrificial fire there with blood.

sanskrit: ke cid yūpān samutpāṭya babhramur vikṛtānanāḥ āsyair anye cāgrasanta tathaiva paricārakān
english: Some, having uprooted the sacrificial posts, roamed about with distorted faces; others devoured with their mouths the very attendants of the rite.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa yajño nṛpate vadhyamānaḥ samantataḥ āsthāya mṛgarūpaṃ vai kham evābhyapatat tadā
english: Then that sacrifice, O lord of men, being assailed on every side, took on the form of a deer and fled up into the sky.

sanskrit: taṃ tu yajñaṃ tathārūpaṃ gacchantam upalabhya saḥ dhanur ādāya bāṇaṃ ca tadānvasarata prabhuḥ
english: But the lord, perceiving the sacrifice fleeing in that shape, took up his bow and an arrow and gave chase.

sanskrit: tatas tasya sureśasya krodhād amitatejasaḥ lalāṭāt prasṛto ghoraḥ svedabindur babhūva ha
english: Then, from the wrath of that lord of gods of measureless splendor, a dreadful drop of sweat issued forth from his brow.

sanskrit: tasmin patitamātre tu svedabindau tathā bhuvi prādurbabhūva sumahān agniḥ kālānalopamaḥ
english: And the instant that drop of sweat fell upon the earth, there arose a vast fire, like the fire of universal dissolution.

sanskrit: tatra cājāyata tadā puruṣaḥ puruṣarṣabha hrasvo 'timātraraktākṣo hariśmaśrur vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: And from it, O bull among men, there was then born a being: short of stature, with eyes exceedingly red, tawny-bearded, and terrifying.

sanskrit: ūrdhvakeśo 'tilomāṅgaḥ śyenolūkas tathaiva ca karālaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaś ca raktavāsās tathaiva ca
english: His hair stood erect, his limbs were thick with hair; hawk- and owl-like was he, gaping-jawed and black of hue, and clothed in red.

sanskrit: taṃ yajñaṃ sa mahāsattvo 'dahat kakṣam ivānalaḥ devāś cāpy adravan sarve tato bhītā diśo daśa
english: That mighty being burned up the sacrifice as a fire burns dry brushwood, and all the gods, stricken with fear, fled then to the ten directions.

sanskrit: tena tasmin vicaratā puruṣeṇa viśāṃ pate pṛthivī vyacalad rājann atīva bharatarṣabha
english: As that being ranged about, O lord of peoples, the earth itself shook violently, O king, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: hāhābhūte pravṛtte tu nāde lokabhayaṃkare pitāmaho mahādevaṃ darśayan pratyabhāṣata
english: When a clamor of "Alas! Alas!" had broken out, a cry that struck terror into the worlds, the Grandsire, addressing Mahādeva, made plain his thought and replied:

sanskrit: bhavato 'pi surāḥ sarve bhāgaṃ dāsyanti vai prabho kriyatāṃ pratisaṃhāraḥ sarvadeveśvara tvayā
english: "To you too, lord, all the gods shall now indeed grant a share; let the withdrawal be made by you, O lord of all the gods."

sanskrit: imā hi devatāḥ sarvā ṛṣayaś ca paraṃtapa tava krodhān mahādeva na śāntim upalebhire
english: "For all these gods and the sages, O scorcher of foes, by reason of your wrath, O Mahādeva, can find no peace."

sanskrit: yaś caiṣa puruṣo jātaḥ svedāt te vibudhottama jvaro nāmaiṣa dharmajña lokeṣu pracariṣyati
english: "And this being who has been born from your sweat, O best of the wise — Fever is his name, O knower of dharma, and as Fever he shall range through the worlds."

sanskrit: ekībhūtasya na hy asya dhāraṇe tejasaḥ prabho samarthā sakalā pṛthvī bahudhā sṛjyatām ayam
english: "For while his fiery force remains gathered into one, the whole earth, O lord, cannot bear it; let him therefore be released in many parts."

sanskrit: ity ukto brahmaṇā devo bhāge cāpi prakalpite bhagavantaṃ tathety āha brahmāṇam amitaujasam
english: Thus addressed by Brahmā, and his share now appointed, the god said "So be it" to the blessed Brahmā of measureless might.

sanskrit: parāṃ ca prītim agamad utsmayaṃś ca pinākadhṛk avāpa ca tadā bhāgaṃ yathoktaṃ brahmaṇā bhavaḥ
english: And the bearer of the Pināka came to supreme delight, smiling broadly; and Bhava then received his share as Brahmā had declared.

sanskrit: jvaraṃ ca sarvadharmajño bahudhā vyasṛjat tadā śāntyarthaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ śṛṇu tac cāpi putraka
english: And the knower of all dharmas then released Fever in many parts, for the welfare of all beings — hear of that too, my son.

sanskrit: śīrṣābhitāpo nāgānāṃ parvatānāṃ śilājatuḥ apāṃ tu nīlikāṃ vidyān nirmokaṃ bhujageṣu ca
english: In elephants it is the burning fever of the head; in mountains, the mineral pitch; in waters one should know it as the green scum, and in serpents as their cast-off slough.

sanskrit: khorakaḥ saurabheyāṇām ūṣaraṃ pṛthivītale paśūnām api dharmajña dṛṣṭipratyavarodhanam
english: In cattle it is the hoof-rot; on the face of the earth, the barren saline soil; and in beasts too, O knower of dharma, it is the dimming of their sight.

sanskrit: randhrāgatam athāśvānāṃ śikhodbhedaś ca barhiṇām netrarogaḥ kokilānāṃ jvaraḥ prokto mahātmanā
english: In horses it is the malady of the orifices; in peacocks, the splitting of the crest; in cuckoos it is declared by the great one to be a disease of the eye — such is Fever.

sanskrit: abjānāṃ pittabhedaś ca sarveṣām iti naḥ śrutam śukānām api sarveṣāṃ hikkikā procyate jvaraḥ
english: In water-born creatures it is the disorder of the bile of them all — so we have heard; and in all parrots, Fever is said to be the hiccup.

sanskrit: śārdūleṣv atha dharmajña śramo jvara ihocyate mānuṣeṣu tu dharmajña jvaro nāmaiṣa viśrutaḥ maraṇe janmani tathā madhye cāviśate naram
english: In tigers, O knower of dharma, it is said here to be weariness as their fever; but among men, O knower of dharma, it is renowned by the very name of Fever, and it enters a man at death, at birth, and in the time between.

sanskrit: etan māheśvaraṃ tejo jvaro nāma sudāruṇaḥ namasyaś caiva mānyaś ca sarvaprāṇibhir īśvaraḥ
english: This is the splendor of Maheśvara, the most dreadful thing named Fever — the lord, to be revered and honored by all living beings.

sanskrit: anena hi samāviṣṭo vṛtro dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ vyajṛmbhata tataḥ śakras tasmai vajram avāsṛjat
english: Possessed by this very Fever, Vṛtra, the best of upholders of dharma, gaped wide; and thereupon Śakra hurled the thunderbolt at him.

sanskrit: praviśya vajro vṛtraṃ tu dārayām āsa bhārata dāritaś ca sa vajreṇa mahāyogī mahāsuraḥ jagāma paramaṃ sthānaṃ viṣṇor amitatejasaḥ
english: Entering into Vṛtra, the thunderbolt rent him asunder, O Bhārata; and that great yogin, the mighty Asura, thus sundered by the thunderbolt, went to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu of measureless splendor.

sanskrit: viṣṇubhaktyā hi tenedaṃ jagad vyāptam abhūt purā tasmāc ca nihato yuddhe viṣṇoḥ sthānam avāptavān
english: For of old, through his devotion to Viṣṇu, this world had been pervaded by him; and therefore, slain in battle, he attained the abode of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: ity eṣa vṛtram āśritya jvarasya mahato mayā vistaraḥ kathitaḥ putra kim anyat prabravīmi te
english: Thus, taking Vṛtra for its occasion, the full account of the great Fever has been told by me, my son. What else shall I declare to you?

sanskrit: imāṃ jvarotpattim adīnamānasaḥ; paṭhet sadā yaḥ susamāhito naraḥ vimuktarogaḥ sa sukhī mudā yuto; labheta kāmān sa yathāmanīṣitān
english: The man who, undaunted in mind and well-composed, ever reads this story of the origin of Fever shall be freed from disease; happy and filled with joy, he shall obtain his desires according to his heart's wish.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śokād duḥkhāc ca mṛtyoś ca trasyanti prāṇinaḥ sadā ubhayaṃ me yathā na syāt tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "From grief, from sorrow, and from death, living beings ever tremble. Tell me, Grandsire, how both of these may be undone for me."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nāradasya ca saṃvādaṃ samaṅgasya ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this very matter they relate an ancient tale, the dialogue of Nārada and Samaṅga, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca uraseva praṇamase bāhubhyāṃ tarasīva ca saṃprahṛṣṭamanā nityaṃ viśoka iva lakṣyase
english: Nārada said: "You seem to bow forward with your very chest, and to push your way through with your arms; ever glad of mind, you appear like one wholly free from grief."

sanskrit: udvegaṃ neha te kiṃ cit susūkṣmam api lakṣaye nityatṛpta iva svastho bālavac ca viceṣṭase
english: "Not the slightest agitation, not even the subtlest, do I discern in you here; ever content and at ease, you behave like a child."

sanskrit: samaṅga uvāca bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyac ca sarvaṃ sattveṣu mānada teṣāṃ tattvāni jānāmi tato na vimanā hy aham
english: Samaṅga said: "What was, what is, and what shall be — all that lies among creatures, O bestower of honor — I know the truths of these; and therefore am I not despondent."

sanskrit: upakramān ahaṃ veda punar eva phalodayān loke phalāni citrāṇi tato na vimanā hy aham
english: "I know undertakings, and likewise the arising of their fruits; the fruits in this world are of many kinds, and therefore am I not despondent."

sanskrit: agādhāś cāpratiṣṭhāś ca gatimantaś ca nārada andhā jaḍāś ca jīvanti paśyāsmān api jīvataḥ
english: "The fathomless and the unsteady, the moving and the wandering, the blind and the dull-witted — all these live, O Nārada; behold us too, that we are living."

sanskrit: vihitenaiva jīvanti arogāṅgā divaukasaḥ balavanto 'balāś caiva tadvad asmān sabhājaya
english: "The dwellers in heaven, sound of limb, live by what is ordained; the strong and the weak alike — so too regard us in like manner."

sanskrit: sahasriṇaś ca jīvanti jīvanti śatinas tathā śākena cānye jīvanti paśyāsmān api jīvataḥ
english: "Those who possess thousands live, and those who possess hundreds live as well; and others live upon mere herbs — behold us too, that we are living."

sanskrit: yadā na śocemahi kiṃ nu na syād; dharmeṇa vā nārada karmaṇā vā kṛtāntavaśyāni yadā sukhāni; duḥkhāni vā yan na vidharṣayanti
english: "When we do not grieve, what then could there be to grieve for, O Nārada, whether through dharma or through action? — since pleasures, being subject to Destiny, and pains likewise, cannot overwhelm us."

sanskrit: yasmai prajñāṃ kathayante manuṣyāḥ; prajñāmūlo hīndriyāṇāṃ prasādaḥ muhyanti śocanti yadendriyāṇi; prajñālābho nāsti mūḍhendriyasya
english: "It is to him men attribute wisdom in whom the serenity of the senses is rooted in wisdom; but when the senses are bewildered and sorrow, there is no winning of wisdom for one whose senses are confounded."

sanskrit: mūḍhasya darpaḥ sa punar moha eva; mūḍhasya nāyaṃ na paro 'sti lokaḥ na hy eva duḥkhāni sadā bhavanti; sukhasya vā nityaśo lābha eva
english: "The pride of the deluded man is but delusion once more; for the deluded there is neither this world nor the world beyond. For pains do not come forever, nor is there a perpetual winning of pleasure."

sanskrit: bhāvātmakaṃ saṃparivartamānaṃ; na mādṛśaḥ saṃjvaraṃ jātu kuryāt iṣṭān bhogān nānurudhyet sukhaṃ vā; na cintayed duḥkham abhyāgataṃ vā
english: "Over this world of becoming, ever revolving in its course, one such as I would never let himself feel torment; he would not crave for cherished enjoyments or for pleasure, nor would he brood over the sorrow that has come upon him."

sanskrit: samāhito na spṛhayet pareṣāṃ; nānāgataṃ nābhinandeta lābham na cāpi hṛṣyed vipule 'rthalābhe; tathārthanāśe ca na vai viṣīdet
english: "Composed, he would not covet what belongs to others, nor would he rejoice over a gain not yet come; he would not exult at a vast acquisition of wealth, nor, when wealth is lost, would he sink into despair."

sanskrit: na bāndhavā na ca vittaṃ na kaulī; na ca śrutaṃ na ca mantrā na vīryam duḥkhāt trātuṃ sarva evotsahante; paratra śīle na tu yānti śāntim
english: "Not kinsmen, not wealth, not high birth, not learning, not sacred counsels, not valor — all these are eager to rescue one from sorrow, yet without character in the life to come they do not attain peace."

sanskrit: nāsti buddhir ayuktasya nāyogād vidyate sukham dhṛtiś ca duḥkhatyāgaś cāpy ubhayaṃ naḥ sukhodayam
english: "For the undisciplined there is no understanding, and without discipline no happiness is found; steadfastness and the renouncing of sorrow — both of these are for us the wellspring of joy."

sanskrit: priyaṃ hi harṣajananaṃ harṣa utsekavardhanaḥ utseko narakāyaiva tasmāt taṃ saṃtyajāmy aham
english: "For what is dear gives rise to elation, elation breeds arrogance, and arrogance leads but to hell; therefore I wholly renounce it."

sanskrit: etāñ śokabhayotsekān mohanān sukhaduḥkhayoḥ paśyāmi sākṣival loke dehasyāsya viceṣṭanāt
english: "These — grief, fear, and arrogance, bewilderers in pleasure and in pain — I behold in the world as a witness might, through the workings of this body."

sanskrit: arthakāmau parityajya viśoko vigatajvaraḥ tṛṣṇāmohau tu saṃtyajya carāmi pṛthivīm imām
english: "Having forsaken wealth and desire, free from grief and rid of fever, having cast off craving and delusion, I wander over this earth."

sanskrit: na mṛtyuto na cādharmān na lobhān na kutaś cana pītāmṛtasyevātyantam iha cāmutra vā bhayam
english: "Neither from death, nor from unrighteousness, nor from greed, nor from any source whatever — like one who has drunk the nectar of immortality, I have no fear at all, here or hereafter."

sanskrit: etad brahman vijānāmi mahat kṛtvā tapo 'vyayam tena nārada saṃprāpto na māṃ śokaḥ prabādhate
english: "This I have come to know, O brāhmaṇa, by performing great and imperishable austerity; and by that attainment, O Nārada, no grief afflicts me."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca atattvajñasya śāstrāṇāṃ satataṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ akṛtavyavasāyasya śreyo brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "For one who does not know the truths of the scriptures, who is forever of doubting mind, who has reached no firm resolve — tell me, Grandsire, what is the highest good."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca gurupūjā ca satataṃ vṛddhānāṃ paryupāsanam śravaṇaṃ caiva vidyānāṃ kūṭasthaṃ śreya ucyate
english: Bhīṣma said: "Constant honoring of one's teacher, attendance upon the elders, and the hearing of the branches of knowledge — this is declared to be the unfailing highest good."

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gālavasya ca saṃvādaṃ devarṣer nāradasya ca
english: "On this too they relate an ancient tale, the dialogue of Gālava and of the divine sage Nārada."

sanskrit: vītamohaklamaṃ vipraṃ jñānatṛptaṃ jitendriyam śreyaskāmaṃ jitātmānaṃ nāradaṃ gālavo 'bravīt
english: To Nārada — a brāhmaṇa freed from delusion and weariness, sated with knowledge, his senses mastered, desiring the highest good and his self subdued — Gālava spoke:

sanskrit: yaiḥ kaiś cit saṃmato loke guṇais tu puruṣo nṛṣu bhavaty anapagān sarvāṃs tān guṇāṃl lakṣayāmy aham
english: "Whatever the virtues by which a man is esteemed in the world among men, all those abiding virtues do I discern in you."

sanskrit: bhavān evaṃvidho 'smākaṃ saṃśayaṃ chettum arhati amūḍhaś ciramūḍhānāṃ lokatattvam ajānatām
english: "You, being such a one, are fit to cut away our doubt — you who are undeluded, for the sake of us long-deluded, who do not know the truth of the world."

sanskrit: jñāne hy evaṃ pravṛttiḥ syāt kāryākārye vijānataḥ yat kāryaṃ na vyavasyāmas tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: "For thus would there be activity grounded in knowledge for one who discerns what should and should not be done; that which we cannot resolve as our duty, you are fit to declare."

sanskrit: bhagavann āśramāḥ sarve pṛthagācāradarśinaḥ idaṃ śreya idaṃ śreya iti nānāpradhāvitāḥ
english: "Blessed lord, all the orders of life teach each its own separate conduct, and each runs off in its own way, crying, 'This is the highest good! This is the highest good!'"

sanskrit: tāṃs tu viprasthitān dṛṣṭvā śāstraiḥ śāstrābhinandinaḥ svaśāstraiḥ parituṣṭāṃś ca śreyo nopalabhāmahe
english: "Seeing them thus set apart by their scriptures, each delighting in his own scripture and content with it, we cannot lay hold of the highest good."

sanskrit: śāstraṃ yadi bhaved ekaṃ vyaktaṃ śreyo bhavet tadā śāstraiś ca bahubhir bhūyaḥ śreyo guhyaṃ praveśitam
english: "Were there but a single scripture, then the highest good would be made plain; but by the many scriptures the highest good has only been driven the deeper into mystery."

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇāc chreyaḥ kalilaṃ pratibhāti mām bravītu bhagavāṃs tan me upasanno 'smy adhīhi bhoḥ
english: "For this reason the highest good appears to me a tangled thicket; let the blessed lord declare it to me — I have come to you as a suppliant; teach me, I pray."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca āśramās tāta catvāro yathāsaṃkalpitāḥ pṛthak tān sarvān anupaśya tvaṃ samāśrityaiva gālava
english: Nārada said: "The orders of life, my dear, are four, each ordained apart; behold them all, Gālava, taking your stand within them."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ teṣāṃ tathā hi tvam āśramāṇāṃ tatas tataḥ nānārūpaguṇoddeśaṃ paśya viprasthitaṃ pṛthak nayanti caiva te samyag abhipretam asaṃśayam
english: "For of each of those several orders, here and there, behold the aim, manifold in form and in quality, set forth apart; and indeed they lead one rightly, without doubt, to the goal intended."

sanskrit: ṛju paśyaṃs tathā samyag āśramāṇāṃ parāṃ gatim yat tu niḥśreyasaṃ samyak tac caivāsaṃśayātmakam
english: "Looking straight and rightly upon the supreme goal of the orders of life — that which is truly the highest blessedness is also the very thing free from all doubt."

sanskrit: anugrahaṃ ca mitrāṇām amitrāṇāṃ ca nigraham saṃgrahaṃ ca trivargasya śreya āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: "The favoring of friends, the restraint of foes, and the holding fast of the threefold aim of life — these the wise call the highest good."

sanskrit: nivṛttiḥ karmaṇaḥ pāpāt satataṃ puṇyaśīlatā sadbhiś ca samudācāraḥ śreya etad asaṃśayam
english: "Turning away from sinful action, a constant habit of virtue, and right conduct in the company of the good — this is the highest good, beyond all doubt."

sanskrit: mārdavaṃ sarvabhūteṣu vyavahāreṣu cārjavam vāk caiva madhurā proktā śreya etad asaṃśayam
english: "Gentleness toward all beings, uprightness in one's dealings, and speech that is sweet — this is declared the highest good, beyond all doubt."

sanskrit: devatābhyaḥ pitṛbhyaś ca saṃvibhāgo 'tithiṣv api asaṃtyāgaś ca bhṛtyānāṃ śreya etad asaṃśayam
english: "Sharing one's portion with the gods, with the ancestors, and with guests too, and never abandoning one's dependents — this is the highest good, beyond all doubt."
